column2: means
column3: remedy -- one row per code tools/build-verdict.sh pairs with a remedy. Tab-separated; lines starting with # are ignored.

column1: # An exact code wins over a prefix row (a code ending in *). The rows keyed exit:... are the verdict's own, for exit codes that print no diagnostic.

column2: A value object, Option or Result made by default
column3: Use the type's factory: From or Create for a value object, Option.Some/Option.None, Result.Success/Result.Failure. default(T), new T() and an unassigned field bypass the rules the type exists for.

column2: A value object compiled without the generators
column3: Reference CodoMetis.TypeKit.Generators from the project that declares the value object; the fabric applies the aspects only where that package is referenced, and without it the type compiles empty.

column2: A Result or Option a call returns is dropped
column3: Handle it (Match, TryGetValue, a continuation) or discard it on purpose with _ =.

column2: Materialize called outside the EF Core satellite
column3: Materialize skips validation and exists for values the application stored itself. Make the value with Create, TryFrom or From; never expose a materializer to input.

column2: A collection filled with default instances
column3: Build the collection from values (OrderId.From(...)); new T[n] and similar fill it with instances no factory made.

column2: A member of a type without a default left unassigned
column3: Assign it in every constructor or mark it required -- the struct counterpart of CS8618.

column2: FromKnownGood called on a value from a parameter
column3: FromKnownGood throws on a value that breaks the rules: right for a constant, wrong for input. Use Create (a Result) or TryFrom (an Option) for anything a caller passes in.

column2: Two value objects compared by unwrapping them
column3: Compare the value objects themselves; unwrapping both sides brings back the mix-up the types prevent. If they are different types, the comparison is the bug.

column2: A call that returns default when it finds nothing
column3: Use the Option-returning form (FirstOrNone, SingleOrNone, GetValueOrNone, ...) instead of FirstOrDefault and friends.

column2: A type argument breaks its parameter's [Abstract], [Record], [Sealed] or [Concrete]
column3: Make the argument satisfy the attribute, or repeat the attribute on the type parameter that forwards it (docs/type-constraints.md).

column2: A type the host constructs by reflection lacks the required parameterless constructor
column3: Add one with the accessibility the attribute asks for; the code fix writes it, except for a type with a primary constructor (docs/type-constraints.md).

column2: A closed set's Match called with positional arguments
column3: Name every argument: Match binds by declaration order, so reordering two members swaps their branches silently.

column2: A closed set's member assigned in its static constructor or another initializer
column3: Initialize each member with new where it is declared, and nowhere else.

column2: A hand-written member the generators introduce
column3: Remove it. Only TryFrom, FromKnownGood, Revalidate, CompareTo(TSelf) and ToString() may be written by hand (the seams); everything else is generated. A new generated member must join this check, or a hand-written one is kept silently.

column2: A declaration the generators refuse, so the type is not generated
column3: The message names the fix; the Generators README's "Build errors" table explains each id. Fix it before any CS or LAMA error on the same type -- those are usually its cascade.

column2: A compiler error inside aspect-generated code
column3: Usually a cascade: fix the CMTK error in the same verdict and rebuild. With no CMTK error, the declaration reached a case the generators do not refuse yet -- that is a missing CMTK rule, not a fix in woven code (design/aspects.md, "Build failures that named nothing the user wrote"). Read the woven code as the Generators README's "Reading the generated code" says.

column2: Metalama's generic note that an aspect probably has a bug
column3: Follows LAMA0611; act on the LAMA0611 or CMTK error in the same verdict.

column2: An aspect threw
column3: A known cause is a C# keyword used as a namespace segment or member name (design/roadmap.md). Otherwise the declaration needs a CMTK rule: reproduce it in BuildOutcomeTests.

column2: Metalama itself failed and took the whole project with it
column3: Find the declaration that triggers it (a file-local value object was one, now CMTK1005) and refuse it with a CMTK rule.

column2: A Metalama diagnostic
column3: Check the CMTK errors in the same verdict first; a Metalama error that names nothing the user wrote is a missing CMTK rule (design/aspects.md). Never use a 2027.0-only Metalama API: the stack is Metalama 2026.1.

column2: Reflection over the interfaces of a Type the trimmer may cut
column3: Never call GetInterfaces(): read GeneratedValueObjectAttribute<TValueObject, T>, whose type arguments are constrained to the interfaces (design/native-aot.md).

column2: A trim or Native AOT warning, an error in the run-time packages
column3: Rewrite, never suppress: no MakeGenericType, no reflection over members the trimmer may remove, no JsonSerializer call that takes only options -- a typed call (GeneratedValueObjectAttribute.Accept, GeneratedJson.TypeInfo) or an interface instead. An [UnconditionalSuppressMessage] needs a measured reason, and the smoke test's aot consumer is the measurement (design/native-aot.md).

column2: Two types of one simple name in one JSON context
column3: Name one: [JsonSerializable(typeof(Shipping.Status), TypeInfoPropertyName = "ShippingStatus")] (docs/native-aot.md).

column2: A public member without XML documentation
column3: Document it: warnings are errors, CS1591 included, on every shipping project.

column2: A member named as its enclosing type
column3: In generated code this is a value object or closed set named as a member the generators introduce: refuse it with CMTK1005 or CMTK1021 rather than renaming in woven code.

column2: Metadata file not found
column3: After the consumer smoke test the restore output points at its packages: run dotnet restore CodoMetis.TypeKit.slnx, then build again.

column2: Unreachable code
column3: When it appears on a seeded defect: a seed that makes a condition constant fails the build as CS0162 or CS8518. Seed a condition that is false at run time instead.

column2: An expression that is always the same value
column3: A seed that makes a pattern constant fails the build; seed a condition that is false at run time instead.

column2: An analyzer built against a newer Roslyn than the compiler running it
column3: The analyzer is then not loaded and every CMTK rule goes silent. The Analyzers project's Microsoft.CodeAnalysis floor stays at 5.0.0 (design/adr/0025): never raise it.

column2: An awaited call that should take the test's CancellationToken
column3: Pass TestContext.Current.CancellationToken; in a throwaway probe file, #pragma warning disable xUnit1051 instead.

column2: A version set in a project while central package management is on
column3: Put the version in Directory.Packages.props. Only spikes/ opts out of central package management.

column2: A package version that no source has
column3: For CodoMetis.TypeKit.* at PackageValidationBaselineVersion, the release just pushed is not on nuget.org yet: wait until https://api.nuget.org/v3-flatcontainer/codometis.typekit/<version>/codometis.typekit.nuspec answers, then run `dotnet nuget locals http-cache --clear`, since restore caches the miss for 30 minutes. For any other package, the version in Directory.Packages.props does not exist.

column2: A direct package reference below what a dependency needs
column3: Raise the direct reference in Directory.Packages.props. The versions of shipping references are floors for consumers, so raising one is a release decision: say so in the change.

column2: A package with a known vulnerability
column3: NU1901-NU1904 stay warnings on purpose (Directory.Build.props). Bump in Directory.Packages.props; for a shipping reference that is a release decision.

column2: The dotnet on PATH cannot satisfy global.json's SDK pin
column3: An environment problem, not a diff problem: put an SDK in the pinned 10.0.4xx band first on PATH (PATH=/usr/local/share/dotnet:$PATH DOTNET_ROOT=/usr/local/share/dotnet). Never edit global.json to match what is installed.

column2: MTP refused the command line and ran nothing
column3:
An option the test hosts do not know. An MSBuild switch (-nodeReuse:false, -p:..., -v:...) after -- is forwarded to every test host, which exits 5: put it on the build instead. The filters are --filter-class, --filter-method, --filter-namespace, --filter-trait, their --filter-not-... forms, --filter-query, or VSTest's --filter; dotnet test --project

--no-build --help lists them.

column2: The filter matched no test
column3: --filter-method and --filter-class match the fully-qualified name: use Namespace.Class.Method or a wildcard (*ProbeTests). A bare method name is a valid filter that matches nothing.

column2: xunit.v3 refused a mix of filter kinds and the host crashed
column3: Use one kind per run: the simple filters (--filter-class, --filter-method, ...), --filter-query, or VSTest's --filter. Mixing them throws before any test runs (measured: exit 134).

column2: A call to an API a platform lacks, reachable on that platform
column3: Guard the call with the platform check the analyzer reads (if (!OperatingSystem.IsWindows()) ...) or mark the member [SupportedOSPlatform]; a test skip such as Assert.SkipWhen is not read as one.
